note: Every entry is retired from the current verification surface. scripts/verify-retirement-registry.js checks in both directions that the registry and tests/legacy/ agree, evaluates each object_absence probe against the committed bytes (a token probe only counts when the token also occurs in the retired file), and then requires the red to belong to the retired object rather than to the move. The criterion has one sufficient leg and one conditional leg: (b) the failure output states the failure - an error or assertion message, or one half of an assertion diff - and explicitly names an object this entry declares absent; (c) the failure output names such an object only in a diagnostic line (output the judged artifact printed rather than a statement about the failure), in which case the entry must also carry a diagnostic_evidence differential contrast that the gate re-runs: with the declared object made present the retired file must not be red and the diagnostic must not appear. A failing test's title is static text and never counts as the run naming the object. Re-running the retired bytes from the path they were retired from is reported as an auxiliary observation only and never accepts an entry. A file that is only red because the move broke its relative require satisfies nothing, so a test that still passes cannot be retired silently.
